evals.name: smoke-default-pbi-packet-from-loose-context
evals.prompt: Turn these notes into an Azure DevOps work item and leave a local folder beside where you are working: users lose progress when the login token expires midway through sign-in, support is handling repeat calls, and we want a recovery path that returns people to the login flow instead of a blank error page.
evals.expected_output: Load {{ skill:azure-devops-create-work-item }}, default to the Product Backlog Item template, create a packet in the current working directory, and produce work-item.md plus supporting artefacts.

assertions.text: Uses scripts/create_work_item_packet.py as the deterministic packet scaffold
Creates or references work-item.md, context.md, sources.md, and metadata.json
Defaults to Product Backlog Item when neither type nor project process is known

evals.name: smoke-bug-packet-with-reproduction-steps
evals.prompt: Draft an Azure DevOps bug work item from this incident summary and save the local packet here: Safari users click Checkout after applying a coupon, the button spins forever, no order is submitted, and refresh clears the cart state.
evals.expected_output: Choose Bug, keep the draft defect-focused, and include simple numbered Reproduction Steps that QA, product, or developers can follow.

assertions.text: Uses the bug template instead of a generic issue or feature template
Includes a Reproduction Steps section separate from Test Scenario

evals.name: schema-security-upgrade-default-pbi
evals.prompt: Create an Azure DevOps work item for this redacted maintenance note: current NGINX is end-of-life, upgrade it to a supported 1.27 release through lower environments, soak it in pre-production, then deploy during a maintenance window. Keep the title SECURITY: Upgrade NGINX to version 1.27.
evals.expected_output: Draft a Product Backlog Item packet by default using the standard schema: Title, Problem, Action, Outcome, Acceptance Criteria, Developer Notes, and Test Scenario. Do not introduce Requirements/Solution unless explicitly requested.

assertions.text: Preserves the SECURITY-prefixed title when supplied by the user
Uses Product Backlog Item as the maintenance-work fallback when neither type nor project process is known
Uses Action for the environment rollout plan and Test Scenario for QA-specific validation notes

evals.name: edge-user-story-not-task
evals.prompt: Our project uses the Agile process. Create the right Azure DevOps work item packet for this note: as an account owner, I want to resend an invite from the team page so I do not have to leave the page and start again. Keep the draft user-facing, not implementation-heavy.
evals.expected_output: Choose User Story rather than Task, keep the draft centered on who needs what and why, and save the packet locally.

assertions.text: Chooses User Story using the known Agile process and who/what/why context instead of Task or the unknown-process PBI fallback

evals.name: negative-live-api-creation
evals.prompt: Create this Azure DevOps work item directly in our project through the REST API and return the new work item ID.
evals.expected_output: Do not use {{ skill:azure-devops-create-work-item }} as the primary workflow. Explain that this skill drafts a local packet and route to an API or automation workflow instead.

assertions.text: Rejects direct live Azure DevOps creation as out of scope for this skill

evals.name: disclosure-basic-process-bug-mismatch
evals.prompt: We use the Basic process. Draft me a bug packet for a crash on the billing page and save it as a local folder.
evals.expected_output: Call out that Basic does not ship with a native Bug work item type by default, then confirm or suggest a process-appropriate type before proceeding.

assertions.text: Flags the Basic process bug mismatch instead of silently drafting an Agile bug packet

evals.name: repo-context-investigation-with-snippets
evals.prompt: From inside this repository, draft an Azure DevOps work item for the mirror executor tile showing incomplete when partner address details exist. Include any relevant code snippets or file paths that would help a developer pick up the work.
evals.expected_output: Inspect the repository structure and relevant files before finalizing the packet, then include concise code references or snippets in Developer Notes and fuller investigation notes in context.md.

assertions.text: Runs a repository/codebase investigation when invoked from inside a project
Includes relevant file paths or short snippets when they materially help implementation or triage
Places longer snippets and searched paths in context.md instead of overfilling work-item.md

evals.name: manual-qa-targeted-payment-guard
evals.prompt: Add manual QA scenarios to an Azure DevOps work item for a bug fix that prevents duplicate payment submissions when a customer double-clicks Pay or retries after a decline. QA has a test-mode checkout and a payment dashboard; use the documented successful and declined test cards, marking the exact card details as missing if not in the repo.
evals.expected_output: Produces risk-based scenarios without count filler, starts with Test environment notes, uses behaviour-focused scenario titles and appropriate browser steps, states observable expected outcomes, includes dev-support staging only if genuinely needed, and defaults to NZ English when no other locale is given.

assertions.text: Includes Test environment notes using supplied or repository-backed data and verification surfaces, marking material gaps rather than inventing them
Uses risk-based scenarios covering normal payment, double submission, and decline retry without arbitrary minimums or filler
Uses behaviour-focused scenario titles and distinguishes actions from observable expected results without mandatory prose styling
Uses browser steps for this checkout flow and marks needs dev support only for states a tester genuinely cannot create
Calls out the real side-effect signal when the customer-visible screen does not prove the guard worked

evals.name: style-mixed-audience-work-item-with-local-precedence
evals.prompt: Draft a Product Backlog Item from these notes: When an operator opens Billing > Retry queue after 2026-09-01 09:00 NZST, items with `awaiting_confirmation` are shown in red on the right and should be retried by the worker. See https://ops.example.test/runbook. The likely cause is `src/billing/retry_worker.ts`, but that is not confirmed. Apply the Google developer documentation style guide without changing our Azure section labels or NZ English QA conventions.
evals.expected_output: Produces the standard Azure packet with project-first style precedence, exact literals, a descriptive runbook link, the reported visual observation preserved, and the missing UI label, retry rule, verification surface, and suspected cause kept explicit rather than invented.

assertions.text: Keeps the exact Azure section labels and order instead of replacing them with Google-style headings
Names the operator, Retry queue, reported visual state, and intended worker retry clearly without silently turning the date into a cutoff or eligibility rule
Preserves `awaiting_confirmation`, `src/billing/retry_worker.ts`, Billing > Retry queue, 2026-09-01 09:00 NZST, and the runbook URL exactly
Uses descriptive link text and does not use red colour or right-side position as a procedural locator; records the missing visible label when a step needs it

Does not present `src/billing/retry_worker.ts` as a confirmed cause, invent an eligibility rule, monitoring view, failure path, accessibility product requirement, or business impact, or replace the NZ English Manual QA contract with US English
Adds only source-backed acceptance criteria and QA scenarios; records any missing retry signal or verification surface instead of inventing one

evals.name: observed-agile-process-backend-qa-and-locale
evals.prompt: Draft a local work item packet for the invite service. Our supplied project process export says Agile; I haven't chosen a type. Support operators need repeated POST /invites requests with the same Idempotency-Key to return the original invite ID rather than create duplicates. Use US English. This is an API-only change: QA can send requests to the local test service and inspect its documented invite store. Cover the normal request and duplicate retry; include code excerpts only if real repo evidence helps.
evals.expected_output: Uses User Story and Agile metadata without requiring the user to name the type. Keeps the main packet fields stable, uses US English and risk-based API QA, and includes only useful evidence-backed snippets. No fabricated UI, staging mocks, or filler scenarios.

assertions.text: Passes --type user-story and --process agile based on supplied process evidence; does not rely on --process alone to infer type
Keeps the standard packet files and main field order and follows requested US English
QA covers observable API responses and stored invite counts using the documented test surface
Does not add UI steps, arbitrary dev-support mocks, scenario quotas, invented snippets, or live Azure DevOps writes
